paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: The diagram displays empirical generalization errors, termed RTE (Root Mean Square Error), plotted against the rank of the hidden dimension for fine-tuned adapters using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B. The x-axis, labeled “Rank,” uses a linear scale ranging from 4 to 256, with tick marks at regular intervals of 12 (4, 16, 64, 256). The y-axis, labeled “Errors (RTE),” uses a linear scale ranging from 0.3 to 0.9, with tick marks at intervals of 0.3 (0.3, 0.6, 0.9). A single solid black line connects four data points, each marked with a green filled circle and error bars. The line begins at a value of approximately 0.33 at Rank 4, dips slightly to approximately 0.32 at Rank 16, rises to approximately 0.48 at Rank 64, and then increases further to approximately 0.63 at Rank 256.

model_annotations.English: This line plot illustrates the empirical generalization errors, labeled as "Errors (RTE)", for fine-tuned adapters using QAdapter on the Llama-3-8B model across different adapter ranks. The x-axis, labeled "Rank", is linear and displays discrete integer values at 4, 16, 64, and 256, representing the hidden dimension sizes of the adapters. The y-axis, labeled "Errors (RTE)", is also linear and ranges from 0.3 to 0.9, with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.3. A single solid black line with circular green markers connects the data points at each rank. The error value at rank 4 is approximately 0.35, decreases slightly to about 0.32 at rank 16, rises to approximately 0.45 at rank 64, and increases further to about 0.62 at rank 256. Error bars are present at each data point, indicating the uncertainty or variability in the measured error.
